name: Hexagonal patterns in honeycomb and basalt columns
summary: Regular hexagonal honeycomb minimizes perimeter for equal-area planar partitions. Basalt columnar joints instead arise from contraction and fracturing during cooling; many columns are hexagonal, but three to seven sides occur. A regular hexagon has 60-degree spacing between successive vertex directions from its center.
source_title: Columnar Jointing — U.S. National Park Service
caveat: Honeycomb perimeter optimization is not itself a bee-building mechanism, and basalt is not literal optimal disk packing. The runtime's 60-degree catalog comparison is an angular coincidence, not evidence of natural cause or a simulation of formation. Basalt fracture junctions are described by 120-degree angles, distinct from 60-degree polar vertex spacing.
